main_text.p: sine ex confess. Haec ille. Extant hujusmodi testimonia trecenta, quæ eos liberare possent ab istac calumnia: sed plura referre necesse non est, præsertim cum Adversarios nostros ipsos, veluti promptissimos Advocatos, accersere possimus. Sed in eo maximè cernitur Adversariorum calumniantium pervicacia, quòd perperam, idque sponte, dissimulant, à Protestantibus, per solam fidem, non tantùm historicam & mortuam, sed vivam, operantem, fiduciam, adeoque salvificam fidem intelligi.

p.i: Pontificiorum ipsorum confessiones, quibus superiores calumnia falsitatis convincuntur.

main_text.head: SECT. IIII.
main_text.p: ETiamsi Adversarii omnes omnium Protestantium libros cribraverint, ut quicquid possint lolii ex eis seligerent, nunquam tamen ex ullo eorum (quod sciam) testimonio potuerunt ostendere, non requiri ab illis necessariò pœnitentiam in iis omnibus qui justificantur. Quid enim de pœnitentia statuerint, unus {t}Bellarminus abunde satis ido-Lib. 1. de pœnitentia, cap. 18.neus relator esse possit: Lutherus docet (inquit) pœnitentiam esse dolorem de peccato, & propositum melioris vitæ. Melanchthon disertis verbis

page.notes: Top left, the first word of the running head is a small abbreviation that I could not read with certainty, so I left it out. The first line of the page is a fragment ("sine ex confess.") and is kept as such. Printed text "Sine" reads as "sine" with a doubtful first letter. The catchword "dicit," and the signature "D d" at the foot are page furniture and are not part of the text. The reference mark "t" in the text and the note in the right margin are the same. Faint show-through from the reverse side is ignored.
